transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess I came in because I’ve just felt down for a long time. It’s like this flat, heavy feeling most days, even when work is fine or people are being nice to me. I still feel kind of empty.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About two years now… a little over that, maybe two years and two months. It started around when that dashboard project at work put me in the spotlight. Since then, it’s just kind of stayed with me.
During those two years, have there been stretches longer than two months when you did not feel down?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady for about two years and two months, since that dashboard project at work put me in the spotlight. I don’t think I’ve had a break from it that lasted more than two months.
During this time, have you ever had a period when the depression became much worse than usual?
I’m not really sure. It’s been pretty consistently low, but I don’t know if I’d say there was a separate period where it got much worse. Nothing stands out like that to me.
During these past two years, have you felt down on most days?
Yeah… most days. It’s like I’ve been carrying this flat, heavy feeling around for a long time. Even when work is going fine or people are nice to me, I still feel down and kind of empty.
Do you feel this started because of the dashboard project at work?
Yeah, I think so. It seems like it started around then—about two years and two months ago—when that dashboard project put me in the spotlight at work.
After that dashboard project ended, did you still feel down?
Yeah. Even after it ended, that feeling didn’t really go away. I still felt down most days—kind of flat and heavy, even when work was okay or people were being nice to me.
At any time during these two years, was there ever a period when your depression was clearly worse than your usual baseline for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. It’s been pretty steady, like a low baseline most of the time. I can’t think of a clear two-week stretch where it got noticeably worse than usual.
How long after that dashboard project ended did your low mood continue?
It pretty much continued the whole time after it ended. I’d say it’s been about two years and two months since that project put me in the spotlight, and the low mood never really lifted.
While you’ve been feeling down, have you also had low energy?

Yeah, definitely. By the afternoon I’m usually really wiped out. Even small work stuff, like fixing a spreadsheet error or finishing expense paperwork, feels like I’m dragging my body and my brain through mud. Even getting myself to soccer can feel like a lot.
During this time, have you been feeling badly about yourself?

Yeah. I tend to feel like I’m not really as capable as people think. Like when coworkers bring up that dashboard I built, instead of feeling proud, my first thought is that I somehow fooled them. And if I miss a follow-up or send an email late, it feels like proof that I’m not actually good at this.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah, it has. At work, my last performance review actually mentioned that I’m missing follow-through now, which was hard to hear. And outside of work, I’ve been dropping things I used to keep up with—soccer commitments, volunteering, even planning for the MBA stuff. It’s like I just don’t stay on top of things the way I used to.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times where things felt harder to enjoy, but I don’t know that I can point to a clear two-week stretch where I just lost interest in everything I usually like.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your sleep was clearly worse than usual?
I’m not sure. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep great, but I don’t know that there was a clear two-week period where my sleep was noticeably worse than usual.
Did this low mood continue for more than six months after the dashboard project ended?
Yeah. It definitely continued more than six months after that. Honestly, it’s been going on about two years and two months now, since that dashboard project put me in the spotlight at work.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your appetite was clearly worse than usual?
I don’t think so. My appetite has gone up and down a little, but I haven’t noticed a clear two-week stretch where it was really worse than usual.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your concentration was clearly worse than usual?
I don’t think I can point to a clear two-week period like that. I’ve had times where it was harder to focus, but I’m not sure it was clearly worse than usual for that long.
Does being in the spotlight at work still feel like an ongoing stressor for you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, work can still feel uncomfortable at times, but I don’t know if I’d say being in the spotlight is an ongoing stressor exactly.
During these past two years, have you had trouble concentrating on most days?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had days where focusing was harder, but I don’t know if I’d say it was most days over the past two years.
During these past two years, have you often felt hopeless?

Yeah, I think I have. I used to make these detailed plans for getting an MBA and moving forward in my career, but lately when I look at them, I just kind of assume I’m not going to get there no matter what I do.
